## Key Ideas {#iv5-key-ideas .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .geometric-lesson }


<div class="g-summary-grid">
<div><h3>Lengths and angle</h3><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|\cos\theta"></span></div><p>Non-zero vectors; state the smaller tail-to-tail angle.</p><div data-geometric="key-angle"></div></div>
<div><h3>Rewrite squared magnitudes</h3><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="|\underset{\sim}{a}|^2=\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{a}"></span></div><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="|\underset{\sim}{a}|=\sqrt{\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{a}}"></span></div><p>Use scalar-product algebra to remove magnitude signs.</p></div>
<div><h3>What the sign tells us</h3><p><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}>0"></span>: the angle is acute (or <span data-math="0^\circ"></span>).</p><p><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}<0"></span>: the angle is obtuse (or <span data-math="180^\circ"></span>).</p></div>
<div><h3>Special cases</h3><p>Same direction: <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|"></span><br>Opposite directions: <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=-|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|"></span><br>Perpendicular: <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=0"></span></p></div>
</div>


::: notes
Revisit the success criterion: for non-zero vectors compare a·b with |a||b|, −|a||b| and 0 to identify same direction, opposite directions and perpendicularity. A positive dot product gives 0°≤θ<90° (acute, or the 0° endpoint); a negative dot product gives 90°<θ≤180° (obtuse, or the 180° endpoint). The sign alone does not establish parallelism. Complete the Section 5 Key Ideas box. The sign summary explicitly includes the 0° and 180° endpoints; each special case displays the complete a·b equality. Although we report the smaller angle in [0°,180°], the reflex angle gives the same dot product since cos(360°−θ)=cos θ. No extra commentary is added to the homework slide.
:::
